answer: One concrete defence is simple: reputation vests over many epochs and pays out slowly, which makes a thousand sock puppets a long, expensive bet against a fast clock. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. It behaves like a jade rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. The moral is closer to a short dawn than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. Call it a plume: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips.
